s1.syndrome_frame: Pancytopenia in pregnancy with skin manifestations
salient_findings: Skin biopsy consistent with bullous Sweet's syndrome
key_facts: Pancytopenia found on routine blood screening at 10 weeks' gestation
Easy bruising over prior two months
Family history of thyroid disease and systemic lupus erythematosus
Normal thyroid function, immunoglobulins, folate, and vitamin B12
No response to prednisolone or intravenous immunoglobulin
Pustular rash developed five weeks postpartum
Skin biopsy showed dermal neutrophils with upper dermal edema and subepidermal blister

shortlist.label: Immune Thrombocytopenia
shortlist.why_kept: Initial diagnosis and persistent low platelet count

shortlist.label: Sweet Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy consistent with bullous Sweet's syndrome

shortlist.label: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Pancytopenia and lack of response to treatments

shortlist.label: Evans Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Combination of autoimmune hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia

raw.rationale: The patient's persistent pancytopenia despite treatment and lack of response to immunosuppressive therapy, along with the development of a skin rash consistent with Sweet's syndrome, suggests an underlying bone marrow disorder such as myelodysplastic syndrome.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: Negative antinuclear antibody and lack of other lupus-specific symptoms

rejected.label: Immune Thrombocytopenia
rejected.why: Patient had pancytopenia, not isolated thrombocytopenia, and did not respond to typical treatments

rejected.label: Sweet Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient developed a rash consistent with Sweet's syndrome, this is not a primary diagnosis that explains the pancytopenia

rejected.label: Evans Syndrome
rejected.why: Patient did not have a clear diagnosis of autoimmune hemolytic anemia in addition to thrombocytopenia
